question.text: Roshni Trust (education-for-disabled NPO, 12AB + 80G registered) expects to receive a USD 2,00,000 grant from a US-based donor. The SIA is doing the pre-engagement compliance sweep. Which registration/clearance is independently required to legally accept the foreign contribution, on top of the 12AB and 80G approvals?

answer.text: No additional clearance — 12AB registration automatically covers foreign contribution
FCRA 2010 registration or prior permission from the Ministry of Home Affairs
SEBI FPI registration — since the inflow is from a foreign source
RBI FEMA declaration filed directly with the Reserve Bank; no MHA involvement

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p.27 of the workbook, the Ministry of Home Affairs regulates foreign contributions under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, and NPOs must register under FCRA to accept foreign donations. FCRA registration (or prior permission) is therefore independently required, in addition to 12AB tax-exempt status and 80G donor approval. Pages 55, 206 and 215 also reference FCRA as a recognised NPO funding source. The Trap: 12AB is an income-tax registration and does not authorise foreign receipts. SEBI FPI registration is for portfolio investors into Indian securities, not for donations. RBI FEMA alone is insufficient because MHA is the lead regulator for foreign contributions. Note: Anchor the answer to the FCRA registration/prior-permission requirement under MHA. The workbook pages checked did not state the SBI Main Branch, New Delhi account or quarterly online-reporting mechanics, so those operational details are not relied on here.
